title: Étale recovery of the closed exceptional quotient comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $1\le m\le n$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, with the quotient map. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. On the ordinary small étale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] let $G_R=Ri_{R,\mathrm{et}}^!$ be the right adjoint to $i_{*,R}$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient], for $R=A,B$. On the pro-étale constructible realization use its transport [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] along $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Put $T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. If $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ (bounded constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with a finite Tor interval: some integers $a\le b$ satisfy $\mathcal H^r(M\otimes_A^LF)=0$ for every degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $F$ and every $r
otin[a,b]$), then both $TG_AM$ and $G_BTM$ are in $D^b_{ctf}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B)$, and the étale exceptional-counit transpose
$$b^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,M}:TG_AM\longrightarrow G_BTM$$
is an isomorphism. Under the tensor pullback and transported exceptional identifications its pullback $
u_Z^*b^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,M}$ equals the pro-étale map of [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek] at $
u_X^*M$. Here the defining transpose is $i_{*,B}TG_AM\xrightarrow{c^{-1}}T i_{*,A}G_AM\xrightarrow{T\varepsilon_A}TM$, where $c$ is the canonical closed-direct-image coefficient comparison. Equality of diagrams between these bounded-below étale outputs can be tested after applying $
u_Z^*$.

proof.text: Write $C_{W,R}=\nu_W^*$, $N=G_AM$ and $M_B=TM$. The schemes $X,Z$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian and its spectrum is quasi-compact. Take the closed case $g=i$, $S=Z$, $j=\mathrm{id}_Z$ of [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek], at the identity coefficient quotient $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,n}$. Its assertion that $N_g=Rg_A^!M$ is finite-Tor bounded constructible gives $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. This uses only that lemma's preservation assertion, not its coefficient isomorphism. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is separated finite type over the fixed $k$, $i$ is closed, $M$ has the stated finite-Tor constructible condition, and $n\ge n\ge1$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: establish the domain of the closed comparison

proof.text: For each of the two inputs $K=M$ on $X$ and $K=N$ on $Z$, choose a Tor interval $[u,v]$ with $u\le v$. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], the Noetherian scheme admits a representative $P\cong K$ of flat constructible $A$-sheaves, zero outside $[u,v]$. By [lem-sf-reduction-flat-model], $P\otimes_A B$ represents $TK$, has flat $B$-terms, and has Tor interval $[u,v]$. Each of its terms is constructible: by the sheafification definition of tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], constant local sections give the local isomorphism $\underline F\otimes_{\underline A}\underline B=\underline{F\otimes_A B}$ (the bilinear map on sections and its inverse on pure tensors glue after sheafification); hence on each stratum and etale cover making $P^r$ constant with finite module value $F$, its tensor is constant with finite $B$-module value $F\otimes_A B$. Finiteness follows because the finitely many elements of $F$ generate this tensor over the finite ring $B$. Thus kernels and cokernels of its differentials, and therefore its cohomology, are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. It is bounded because its terms vanish outside $[u,v]$. Consequently $M_B$ and $TN$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible over $B$. No flatness of $B$ over $A$ is used.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: quotient reduction on finite-Tor constructible inputs

proof.text: Apply the same preservation assertion of [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek] with coefficient level $m$, its identity quotient $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,m}$, and input $M_B$. This gives $G_BM_B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. The two requested etale outputs are therefore already bounded below. By [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], the pullbacks of $M,N,M_B,TN,G_BM_B$ are bounded constructible with their respective finite Tor intervals. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the comparison with constant $A$ coefficients and to the constant module $B$, write $t_{W,K}:C_{W,B}(TK)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{p}C_{W,A}K$ for the canonical $B$-linear tensor identification. The module action is the pulled-back constant $B$ action. By the definition of the transported exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], its value on $C_{X,R}L$ identifies with $C_{Z,R}G_RL$ for $L=M$ over $A$ and $L=M_B$ over $B$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: identify the two sites and check all output categories

proof.text:
For $R=A,B$, let $\delta_{R,Q}:C_{X,R}i_{*,R}^{e}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{*,R}^{p}C_{Z,R}Q$ be [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. It applies to bounded-below $Q$, because [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies inverse images of affine opens with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The diagonal is an isomorphism (on these charts $(R/I)\otimes_R(R/I)=R/I$), hence quasi-compact; so $i$ is quasi-separated. The same charts show finite type (a quotient needs no algebra generators) and separatedness (the isomorphism diagonal is closed). Let $c^e:T i_*^eN\to i_*^eTN$ and $c^p:T^pi_*^pC_{Z,A}N\to i_*^pT^pC_{Z,A}N$ be the ordinary coefficient maps of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. That theorem applies: $N$ is etale finite-Tor constructible, $i$ is separated finite type, and $B$ is cyclic, hence finite as an $A$-module. The two maps from $C_{X,B}Ti_*^eN$ to $i_*^pT^pC_{Z,A}N$ agree:
$$i_*^p(t_{Z,N})\,\delta_{B,TN}\,C_{X,B}(c^e)=c^p\,T^p(\delta_{A,N})\,t_{X,i_*N}.$$
Indeed transpose through the ordinary $B$-coefficient $i_p^*\dashv i_*^p$. The defining transpose of $c$ is the coefficient extension of the ordinary pullback counit. The defining normalization of $\delta$ carries the etale pullback counit to the pro-etale one. Under [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the tensor identification of step 3, both transposes are therefore the coefficient extension of $C_{Z,A}(i_e^*i_*^eN\to N)$. At flat representatives the tensor identification sends $x\otimes b$ to the pulled-back $x\otimes b$, so applying the counit before or after this identification gives that same map. Injectivity of the Hom adjunction proves the equation; equivalently it is the pasting identity of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting].

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: ordinary direct-image coefficient square on the two sites

proof.text:
The exceptional counit under transport is normalized as follows. For bounded-below etale $Q,L$ in the domains here, the comparison $\delta$ and full faithfulness of $C_R$ give the successive natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{p}(i_*^pC_{Z,R}Q,C_{X,R}L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{e}(i_*^eQ,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{e}(Q,G_RL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{p}(C_{Z,R}Q,C_{Z,R}G_RL).$$
Use [lem-exc-closed-ambient] for the middle bijection and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] for the other Hom identifications. This is the transported adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Set $Q=G_RL$ and take the identity in the last Hom set. Its preimage is exactly
$$\varepsilon_R^p=C_{X,R}(\varepsilon_R^e)\,\delta_{R,G_RL}^{-1}.$$
The rule that the counit is this preimage of the identity is [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Thus this equation identifies the specified counit, not merely the right-adjoint objects. It applies at $(R,L)=(A,M)$ and $(B,M_B)$ by steps 1--3; all four Hom arguments are bounded below.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: transported exceptional adjunction and its counit

proof.text:
Let $\widetilde b$ be $C_{Z,B}(b^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,M})$ conjugated by the tensor and exceptional identifications of step 3. Transpose it under the transported $i_{*,B}^p\dashv G_B^p$. By step 5 its transpose, with source identified with $i_{*,B}^pC_{Z,B}TN$, is
$$C_{X,B}(T\varepsilon_A^e)\,C_{X,B}((c^e)^{-1})\,\delta_{B,TN}^{-1}.$$
Here the defining etale transpose is used exactly as written in the statement. Step 4, inverted on the coefficient comparisons, rewrites this as $T^p(C_{X,A}\varepsilon_A^e)\,T^p(\delta_{A,N}^{-1})\,(c^p)^{-1}$, after the canonical tensor identifications. Naturality of those identifications justifies their passage through the counit. By step 5 this is $(T^p\varepsilon_A^p)(c^p)^{-1}$. It is precisely the defining transpose of the pro-etale map in [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek]. Injectivity of this exceptional Hom bijection proves that $\widetilde b$ is that map. This calculation uses only bounded constructible etale-origin source objects; it never asserts an adjunction on all pro-etale complexes.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: identify the exceptional-counit transposes

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek] now hold for the quotient $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ and the pro-etale input $C_{X,A}M$: step 3 gave its finite-Tor constructibility, $i$ is a closed immersion between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and the prime is invertible in $k$. Thus the pro-etale map identified in step 6 is an isomorphism. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], $C_{Z,B}$ is fully faithful on $D^+$, which contains both etale outputs by steps 2--3. It reflects this isomorphism explicitly: lift the inverse of its image using fullness; faithfulness applied to the two inverse equations makes that lift an inverse to $b^{\mathrm{et}}_{i,M}$. Finally, for any two paths in a diagram between these bounded-below outputs, equal images under $C_{Z,B}$ imply equal paths by faithfulness. This proves both the etale isomorphism and the asserted test for equality of diagrams.
